h: Tips for a brilliant day in Wrexham
p: Xplore! works best when you let curiosity take the lead. Rather than marching round every zone in order, let the kids pick what grabs them and come back to the rest. Mixed-age families do well here because the exhibits work on different levels: toddlers enjoy the colours and buttons, while older children can dig into how things actually work. Grown-ups, be warned, you will end up having a go yourselves.

Plan for a couple of hours, more if there's a show or workshop on. Weekdays in term time can see school groups visiting, so if you're after a quieter session, weekends and holiday afternoons are worth comparing. And because it sits right in the city centre, it's easy to break the visit up with lunch out and come back refreshed.

Once the experimenting's done, Wrexham has plenty to keep you busy. Tŷ Pawb, the arts centre and market hall with its food court, is a lively spot for a bite and a browse. Wrexham Museum on Regent Street tells the story of the area, football included, and the Racecourse Ground, home of Wrexham AFC, has become famous well beyond Wales. Fancy fresh air? The National Trust's Erddig estate is just south of the city, with gardens and parkland to roam, and the spectacular Pontcysyllte Aqueduct is a short drive away near Trevor, perfect for a walk across the sky on a fine day.
